# National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM) – Summary
The National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM), founded in 1910, is Mexico's largest and most prominent university. Created as a secular institution aiming to unify and expand higher education in Mexico City, it officially gained autonomy in 1929, allowing it to independently govern academic affairs. UNAM's main campus, Ciudad Universitaria in southern Mexico City, was completed in 1954 and designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007. The university operates numerous satellite campuses across Mexico and extension schools internationally in the United States, Canada, Europe, China, and Costa Rica. UNAM also manages important cultural and research institutions, museums, and libraries, including the National Museum (Museo Nacional) and the National Astronomical Observatory.
Academically, UNAM is organized into schools and colleges offering undergraduate and graduate degrees, with a student body exceeding 324,000, and runs preparatory schools and science high schools in Mexico City. It is consistently ranked as Mexico's top university and as one of Latin America's leading institutions. Renowned for its research output, UNAM accounts for more than half of Mexico's scientific production and hosts major research institutes in fields ranging from physics and biotechnology to astronomy and robotics. UNAM has a robust international faculty and attracts students and researchers worldwide. Its contributions to Artificial Intelligence, robotics, and other fields have been recognized globally.
Culturally and politically, UNAM is known for its rich traditions, activism, and inclusivity, supporting minorities and fostering innovation and social change. The university's seal and motto, "For my people the spirit shall speak," reflect its humanistic mission and Latin American identity. Its sports teams, notably Club Universidad Nacional (Pumas) and the Pumas CU, play a central role in Mexican athletics. UNAM's alumni include three Nobel laureates, several Mexican presidents, and leading figures in science, arts, business, and public service, affirming the university's pivotal role in national and international spheres.
